summary: Monroe County, AL 120-foot International Derrick tower started by the CCC and finished by the Alabama Forestry Commission in 1941; last manned until 1981; NHLR US 854.

facts.design: 120-foot International Derrick tower with sun visors on the cab
facts.status_note: A blog links videos shot in 2016 and December 2020; no source gives its condition since then

access.note: No public access information found. The blog says the tower was closed after 1981 but does not say whether that means closed to the public

events.note: Started by the CCC and completed by the Alabama Forestry Commission in 1941, per the Register
Last manned by Forest Ranger Colbert Wright of Excel, who retired in 1981, per the blog
Blog says the tower was closed after the retirement due to budget restrictions
Registered December 18, 2009 as US 854, AL 32; nominated by Thomas Kaufmann

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register lists AL 32 and the blog lists AL 33. The story follows the Register, the source that issues the number.

notes_for_editor: Staffing (last manned by Colbert Wright, retired 1981) and the 1981 closure rest on one blog post, so the story attributes them to the blog. The blog is also the only source for the 2016 and December 2020 videos; the Vimeo video page was blocked by a verification wall, and its 'abandoned' description seen in search results is not used. The 120-foot height is read from the Register's phrase 'one of the few remaining 120' towers', not from a measured figure. The brief's 'standing' status is kept on the strength of the 2020 videos, but no current condition is confirmed. Access is unknown; the story advises checking with the Alabama Forestry Commission and does not encourage climbing.
